title: Atacama star trails
caption: Star trails around the celestial south pole over the Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The whole sky seems to pivot around one spot, the celestial south pole, leaving curving star trails behind it. Closer to home, distant orange glows mark where people live around the Chilean Atacama Desert. The photograph is by Carlos A. Durán.

The swirl is an effect of Earth's rotation. Because the planet spins on its axis, the whole sky appears to turn around the celestial poles. Over a long exposure, each star traces an arc around that center, and the arcs grow larger for stars farther from the pole.

The orange glows tell a different story. They come from towns and settlements, whose lights brighten the sky above them. Even in the Atacama, human light shows up in the picture, and dark skies are easily brightened.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera in the Atacama Desert. The exposure settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points. Only a long exposure records their motion around the pole as trails.

explore: The celestial south pole is the point in the sky directly above Earth's South Pole, and it is only visible from the Southern Hemisphere.
alt: Star trails circling a single point in the sky, with distant orange glows from human settlements.
